a: Several women made significant contributions to Renaissance art despite facing immense barriers to training and professional recognition. Artemisia Gentileschi (1593-1656) was one of the most accomplished painters of the Baroque period, known for her powerful depictions of women from history and mythology, such as 'Judith Slaying Holofernes.' She was the first woman admitted to the Accademia di Arte del Disegno in Florence. Sofonisba Anguissola (c. 1532-1625) was an Italian Renaissance painter who gained international fame for her portraits and self-portraits. She served as a court painter to King Philip II of Spain and was praised by Michelangelo. Lavinia Fontana (1552-1614) was a Bolognese painter who is considered the first woman artist to earn a living from her work, supporting her family through commissions. Properzia de' Rossi (c. 1490-1530) was a Bolognese sculptor who worked in marble, one of the few female sculptors of the Renaissance. Plautilla Nelli (1524-1588) was a Florentine nun and painter who created large-scale religious works, including a famous 'Last Supper.' These women overcame significant restrictions on their education and access to life drawing classes to create enduring works of art.

Urban gardening is the practice of growing plants, vegetables, herbs, and fruits in city environments where space is limited. For beginners, here are the key steps to get started. First, assess your available space: a balcony, rooftop, windowsill, or small yard. Even a single pot on a windowsill can grow herbs. For vegetables, choose a spot that receives at least 6 hours of direct sunlight daily. Container gardening is ideal for urban spaces — use pots, grow bags, or raised beds with drainage holes and quality potting soil, not garden soil. Start with easy-to-grow plants like lettuce, spinach, cherry tomatoes, peppers, basil, mint, strawberries, and radishes. Water consistently — containers dry out faster than ground soil, so check daily and water when the top inch of soil feels dry. Use organic fertilizers and consider vertical gardening techniques like trellises, wall planters, and hanging baskets to maximize space. For soil, use a mix of potting soil and compost. Urban gardeners should also consider joining community gardens for access to more space and shared knowledge. Common challenges include limited sunlight, wind on balconies, and pollution, which can be mitigated by choosing appropriate plants and using barriers.
